We need to generate JUnit 4 test cases for HttpStatusException. Must start with ###Test START## and end with ###Test END##. Tests should comprehensively test all methods: constructor, getters, toString. Also test inheritance from IOException, behavior of message, that toString includes super.toString and status, url. Edge cases: null url, empty string, negative status code, zero, large. Also test that getMessage returns message from super. Also test that toString format exactly matches expectation. Should also test serializable? Not needed.

We'll create a test class HttpStatusExceptionTest in same package org.jsoup. Use assertEquals, assertNull, assertTrue. For toString, we need to capture super.toString which includes class name + message. The super.toString returns getClass().getName() + ": " + getMessage(). Since subclass overrides toString but calls super.toString() which will be HttpStatusException's toString from IOException? Actually super.toString() refers to IOException's toString (which inherits from Throwable). That includes class name (java.io.IOException) or subclass? Actually Throwable.toString uses getClass().getName() which for HttpStatusException (since we are in subclass) but super.toString() called from subclass will still use the subclass's class? Implementation: public String toString() { String s = getClass().getName(); String message = getLocalizedMessage(); return (message != null) ? (s + ": " + message) : s; } So calling super.toString() from subclass still uses the subclass's class (HttpStatusException) because getClass() returns runtime class. So super.toString() will be "org.jsoup.HttpStatusException: message". So toString returns that + ". Status=code, URL=url". We'll test that.

Edge case: message null? The constructor passes message to super; if null, getMessage returns null, super.toString returns just class name. So test.

Also test that getters return stored values.
